condition: Single-shell b1000 DTI with num_b1000 >= 15, bvec condition number <= 2.5, SNR about 30-55, and near-isotropic voxels <= 1.25 mm
model: Spatial UNet/CNN with residual/group-norm encoding and channel+spatial attention is a strong default when preserving spatial detail is important.
Voxelwise MLP can also work when denoising is available and no thick-slice anisotropy is present; avoid very large/irregular MLP expansion unless needed.
data: Use normalize_b0_mean as the default normalization.
Use MPPCA when signal has visible noise or clipping/skew, but avoid heavy added noise augmentation.
Axial slicewise sampling is often safer for spatial models; voxelwise sampling is viable for compact MLP regimes.
training: AdamW with warmup_plateau is a stable default for spatial models.
Use moderate slicewise batches around 20-32 for spatial models; voxelwise MLPs can use much larger batches when memory allows.
Use early stopping with long patience rather than short reactive stopping.
loss: Keep MSE dominant with only small MAE/Huber/Rician/SSIM auxiliaries.
Use light or zero TV; keep coordinate finite-difference and bending penalties off.
Manual shell weighting can help, but avoid extreme b0 dominance unless the baseline shell is clearly underfit.
boundary: Does not cover sparse 6-direction or ill-conditioned bvec sets.
High SNR alone does not justify voxelwise modeling when slices are thick or angular sampling is poor.

condition: Single-shell b1000 DTI with num_b1000 around 6 or bvec condition number >= 5, SNR >= 30
model: Prefer models with spatial context or moderate voxelwise MLPs over coordinate/hash-grid implicit models.
For slicewise use, compact UNet/CNN/Swin-style attention can help stabilize poor angular conditioning.
data: Use MPPCA denoising when available.
Use normalize_b0_mean unless b0 intensity clipping or median-stable high dynamic range suggests normalize_b0_median.
Keep augmentation absent or very light; avoid strong flips/rotations/noise when angular information is already sparse.
training: Use AdamW with conservative gradient clipping and long schedules.
For attention or token models, reduce slicewise batch size early to avoid memory-driven failures.
loss: Use manual shell weighting to prevent the single diffusion shell from being washed out.
Keep robust auxiliaries modest; do not replace MSE with heavily Huber/Rician-dominant losses.
Keep TV tiny or zero unless using slicewise attention, where only a very small TV buffer is useful.
boundary: If num_b1000 >= 15 and condition number < 2.5, less robust/spatial compensation is needed.
Very high bvec condition numbers do not make coordinate smoothness penalties reliable.

condition: Anisotropic spatial resolution with through-plane voxel size about 3.0 mm and in-plane voxel size <= 1.0 mm, single-shell b1000, SNR >= 100
model: Favor axial slicewise spatial UNet/CNN with residual/group-norm blocks and attention over voxelwise MLP.
Avoid memory-heavy window/token attention unless batch size is reduced substantially.
data: Use axial orientation to align slices with the thick-slice acquisition.
Use normalize_b0_mean.
Use no augmentation or only mild geometric augmentation; avoid added noise.
training: Warmup_plateau with AdamW is more reliable than restart-style schedules.
Moderate slicewise batches around the 20s-40s are preferred.
loss: Use MSE-dominant reconstruction with small Huber/SSIM and optional very light TV.
Rician terms are optional and should remain small.
boundary: This does not imply spatial UNet is always better for isotropic 2.0-2.5 mm scans.
If only voxelwise processing is feasible, compensate with MPPCA and conservative losses.

condition: Single-shell b1000 DTI with SNR <= 25, b0_WM_to_GM_ratio <= 0.70, and bvec condition number >= 6
model: Use spatial/operator/window models or moderately sized voxelwise MLPs; avoid oversized MLPs and coordinate hash grids.
If using slicewise models, keep width moderate rather than scaling attention aggressively.
data: MPPCA is strongly useful.
Consider normalize_b0_median when b0 distribution is clipped or highly skewed; otherwise normalize_b0_mean remains acceptable.
Use little to no augmentation; if augmentation is needed, prefer noise-only at very low probability.
training: Use conservative AdamW settings and long schedules.
Avoid overly loose gradient clipping in low-SNR/ill-conditioned regimes.
loss: Use manual shell weighting with moderate b0 emphasis or balanced b0/diffusion weights.
Use mixed MSE+Huber with small Rician; avoid heavy TV and coordinate penalties.
boundary: When SNR is high and bvec condition number < 3, do not over-regularize based on this low-SNR rule.
Manual shell weighting should not become extreme enough to suppress diffusion residuals.

condition: Multi-shell DKI with b1000 and b2000, num_b1000 >= 10, num_b2000 >= 20, shell bvec condition numbers < 2.2, near-isotropic voxels <= 1.25 mm, and SNR about 30-55
model: Use high-capacity spatial/token models rather than coordinate/hash-grid implicit models.
Token Mamba is strong when signal scale is stable and memory supports patch/slicewise training; spatial CNN/UNet is safer when SNR is lower or signal is more heterogeneous.
Avoid VAE/KL variants by default.
data: Use MPPCA denoising.
Use normalize_b0_mean as the first choice unless median normalization is specifically supported by clipping/skew statistics.
Use slicewise axial or coronal orientation according to memory and spatial shape; avoid coordinate representations.
training: AdamW with warmup_plateau and long patience is a stable default.
Use reduced batches for token/window models; memory feasibility should override larger-batch preferences.
Use conservative gradient clipping for token models.
loss: Use manual shell weighting with increasing emphasis on higher b-shells.
Use MSE plus meaningful Huber/MAE but keep SSIM tiny and TV light.
Use a nonzero DKI physics constraint, but avoid letting the constraint dominate optimization.
boundary: Sparse 6-direction shells require stronger robustness and often different model capacity.
Coarse 2.5 mm scans may favor voxelwise MLP even with well-conditioned shells.

condition: DKI with sparse shells: num_b1000 <= 6 and num_b2000 <= 6, shell bvec condition numbers >= 4.5, SNR about 30-55
model: Prefer compact token/window-attention or spatial models with spatial context over coordinate models.
Do not scale token/window models aggressively; moderate width/depth is safer.
data: Use MPPCA denoising.
Slicewise processing is generally safer than coordinate/hash-grid training.
Use only mild augmentation; avoid strong noise or rotations.
training: Use AdamW with warmup_plateau, long warmup, and conservative clipping.
Reduce batch size proactively for attention/token families.
loss: Use manual shell weighting, often with substantial high-shell emphasis.
Use mixed MSE/Huber/MAE with low Rician and very small SSIM.
Use light TV; avoid coordinate finite-difference regularization.
boundary: If bvec condition numbers are < 2 and directions are >= 10/20, do not overemphasize sparse-shell compensation.
Very high high-shell weights can destabilize sparse high-b residuals.

condition: Coarse DKI with voxel size about 2.5 mm isotropic, brain patch about 53x66x54, SNR around 35, and well-conditioned shells with num_b1000 >= 10, num_b2000 >= 20, condition numbers < 2.2
model: Large but controlled voxelwise MLPs become competitive and may outperform slicewise models.
Avoid KAN or extremely wide/deep voxelwise variants unless memory and stability are proven.
data: Use voxelwise data with MPPCA and normalize_b0_mean.
Use no augmentation.
training: Use smaller voxelwise batches than maximum memory permits; moderate batches improve feasibility for high-capacity MLPs.
Cosine_warmup with long decay is a strong option for tuned voxelwise MLPs.
loss: Use Huber-leaning mixed reconstruction with reduced pure MSE dominance.
Use lower b0 and higher high-b shell weights, but keep ratios moderate.
Use zero TV and no coordinate penalties.
boundary: Sparse 6-direction coarse scans may favor token/slicewise models instead.
Near-isotropic high-resolution scans should not automatically use voxelwise MLPs.

condition: Coarse DKI with voxel size about 2.5 mm isotropic, sparse shells with num_b1000 <= 6 and num_b2000 <= 6, condition numbers >= 5, and SNR around 35
model: Moderate token Mamba models are useful; avoid very large Mamba/window variants.
Non-VAE token models are safer than VAE/KL variants.
data: Use MPPCA denoising and normalize_b0_median when signal dynamic range is large.
Coronal or axial slicewise orientation can work; choose orientation that improves memory and slice coverage.
Use very light augmentation only.
training: Use AdamW with warmup_plateau, small learning rate, and moderate gradient clipping.
Slicewise batches can be larger than high-resolution token settings but should still be kept within safe memory limits.
loss: Use balanced manual shell weighting with only mild high-shell upweighting.
Use MSE-dominant reconstruction with moderate Huber and small Rician.
Use low-to-moderate TV, not zero-heavy coordinate regularization.
boundary: If shells are well-conditioned and have many directions, voxelwise MLP may be more efficient.
Aggressive high-shell weighting is risky with only 6 directions per shell.

condition: DKI signal with b0 mean < 500 and SNR about 30-35, multi-shell b1000/b2000, near-isotropic high-resolution voxels around 1.05 mm
model: Spatial CNN/UNet with residual/group-norm attention is safer than large token models when signal scale is low and heterogeneous.
Avoid coordinate/hash-grid implicit models.
data: Use MPPCA denoising.
Use normalize_b0_mean as default in low-intensity scans.
Coronal slicewise orientation can be useful for spatial CNNs.
training: Use AdamW with warmup_plateau and moderate learning rates.
Use conservative gradient clipping and long patience.
loss: Use manual shell weighting with high-shell emphasis.
Use balanced MSE/Huber/MAE/Rician and small TV.
DKI constraint weights may need to be larger than in high-SNR token settings.
boundary: High signal-scale 3T scans with b0 mean in the thousands may favor token Mamba or voxelwise MLP.
Do not combine large constraint weights with very high TV or heavy robust losses.

condition: NODDI with 3 diffusion shells including b3000, num_b1000/b2000/b3000 >= 15 each, shell condition numbers < 2.0, SNR about 35-55
model: Voxelwise MLP is a strong default; compact KAN voxelwise MLP can help on coarse 2.5 mm data.
Use slicewise token/spatial models only when voxelwise MLP underfits or memory is favorable.
data: Use MPPCA denoising.
Use no augmentation for voxelwise training.
normalize_b0_median can help when high dynamic range or clipping is present; normalize_b0_mean is safer for KAN voxelwise settings with stable b0 scaling.
training: Use long training schedules with AdamW and conservative clipping.
For KAN voxelwise models, use moderate batches in the thousands to low ten-thousands rather than extremely large voxelwise batches.
loss: Use manual shell weighting that downweights b0, emphasizes b1000/b2000, and does not overemphasize b3000.
Use MSE plus strong Huber contribution with small MAE/Rician.
Use zero TV and no coordinate regularization for voxelwise models.
boundary: Sparse 6-direction shells require different shell weighting and may favor token/window slicewise models.
Do not let b3000 dominate the loss even when it is present.

condition: NODDI with b1000 and b2000 only, well-conditioned shells with num_b1000 >= 10, num_b2000 >= 20, condition numbers < 2.2, SNR about 30-55
model: Voxelwise MLP is generally preferred over slicewise spatial or coordinate/hash-grid models.
Moderate-width MLPs are safer than very large/deep MLPs.
data: Use MPPCA denoising.
normalize_b0_mean is a strong default for voxelwise fitting.
Use no augmentation.
training: Use AdamW with long schedules and either cosine_warmup or warmup_plateau depending on stability.
Use large voxelwise batches when using plain MLPs, but avoid pushing to memory limits.
loss: Use MSE-dominant or MSE/Huber-balanced reconstruction with modest MAE/Rician.
Use manual shell weighting with low b0 weight and moderate b1000/b2000 emphasis.
Use zero TV and no coordinate penalties.
boundary: Coarse scans with attention models may benefit from tiny TV, but this does not transfer to voxelwise MLP.
If bvec condition numbers rise above 5 with only 6 directions per shell, use sparse-shell guidance instead.

condition: NODDI with sparse b1000/b2000 shells, num_b1000 <= 6 and num_b2000 <= 6, shell condition numbers >= 4.5, SNR about 30-55
model: Voxelwise MLP remains reliable; compact KAN MLP can help for coarse 2.5 mm data.
For slicewise alternatives, token Mamba or compact window attention is preferable to heavy spatial CNNs or coordinate grids.
data: Use MPPCA denoising.
Use no augmentation for voxelwise models; for slicewise models, keep augmentation absent or extremely light.
normalize_b0_mean works well for low-intensity or KAN voxelwise regimes; normalize_b0_median can help in high dynamic-range slicewise/token regimes.
training: Use conservative AdamW and long schedules.
Use tight gradient clipping, especially for KAN or token models.
Avoid very large KAN batches; moderate batches are safer.
loss: Use manual shell weighting with b0 strongly downweighted and diffusion shells emphasized.
Avoid excessive highest-shell emphasis.
Use Huber/MSE mixtures with small Rician and no TV for voxelwise models.
boundary: If shells are dense and well-conditioned, larger plain voxelwise MLPs may be sufficient without KAN.
Slicewise TV should remain zero or tiny; heavy TV harms parameter recovery.

condition: NODDI with single b0, b0 p99 equal to or near scanner maximum or strong b0 clipping, SNR about 35-55
model: Voxelwise MLP or compact window/token slicewise models are safer than coordinate/hash-grid models.
Avoid unnecessarily large model expansion because clipping reduces useful intensity information.
data: MPPCA denoising is important.
normalize_b0_median is often preferable when clipping/skew is evident.
Avoid noise augmentation that compounds clipped-signal artifacts.
training: Use cosine_warmup or warmup_plateau with long warmup and tight clipping.
Use early stopping only with long patience.
loss: Use mixed MSE+Huber with small Rician, not pure MSE.
Downweight b0 relative to diffusion shells when b0 clipping is strong.
Keep TV and coordinate penalties off unless using a compact slicewise attention model with tiny TV.
boundary: If b0 distribution is not clipped and intensity scale is low, normalize_b0_mean may outperform median normalization.
Median normalization is not a substitute for denoising.

condition: Coarse NODDI with voxel size about 2.5 mm isotropic and SNR about 35, multi-shell data with at least b1000 and b2000
model: Compact voxelwise KAN MLPs are useful for voxelwise fitting, especially when shell sampling is sparse.
Compact CSWin/window attention can be competitive for slicewise median-normalized data, but keep it memory-safe.
data: Use MPPCA denoising.
Use no augmentation for voxelwise KAN; no or minimal augmentation for slicewise attention.
Choose normalize_b0_mean for KAN voxelwise settings; choose normalize_b0_median when slicewise high-dynamic-range attention models are used.
training: Use AdamW with small learning rate, tight clipping, and long patience.
Use batches around 7k-12k for KAN voxelwise models under 35-40 GB memory rather than very large batches.
Use small slicewise batches for attention models.
loss: Use manual shell weights that strongly emphasize b1000/b2000 and keep b0 low.
For 3-shell data, keep the highest shell moderate rather than dominant.
Use zero TV for voxelwise KAN; only tiny TV for slicewise attention.
boundary: Fine-resolution 1.25 mm dense-shell NODDI may prefer larger plain MLPs instead of KAN.
KAN/token models become memory-risky if batch or width is scaled aggressively.

condition: NODDI with very high SNR >= 250, single-shell or limited-shell data, and 2.0 mm isotropic voxels
model: Moderate voxelwise MLPs are strong; spatial CNNs can work but are not the default.
Avoid coordinate/hash-grid models with coordinate smoothness penalties.
data: normalize_b0_mean is a safe default.
Denoising is less critical than in SNR <= 55 regimes, but normalization consistency remains important.
Use no augmentation for voxelwise training.
training: Use AdamW with moderate learning rate and conservative clipping.
Long schedules are useful, but avoid over-large models that exploit high SNR by overfitting.
loss: MSE with modest MAE/Huber is sufficient; Rician can be omitted or kept tiny.
Use manual shell weighting to emphasize diffusion shells more than b0.
Keep SSIM, TV, and coordinate penalties off.
boundary: High SNR does not remove the need for denoising/robustness in clipped or sparse bvec data.
For multi-shell b3000 NODDI, use the multi-shell shell-weighting guidance instead.

condition: Any DKI dataset with MPPCA-denoised multi-shell signals and no severe slice anisotropy, where b0 mean is stable and shell means decrease monotonically with b-value
model: Avoid VAE/KL variants by default across spatial, token, and window families.
Prefer non-KAN standard token/window/spatial models unless voxelwise KAN has a clear memory-safe role.
data: Keep augmentation light; denoising and shell balancing are more useful than synthetic noise.
Prefer slicewise or voxelwise representations over coordinate/hash-grid representations.
training: Use AdamW rather than Adam for mature high-capacity configurations.
Prefer warmup_plateau for token/spatial DKI unless a tuned voxelwise MLP regime supports cosine_warmup.
loss: Manual shell weighting is preferred over inverse-volume/default shell weighting.
Use only light TV and no coordinate finite-difference/bending penalties.
Use DKI constraint weights as a stabilizer, not as the dominant objective.
boundary: Voxelwise coarse DKI can favor cosine_warmup and zero TV.
Very low SNR or low signal-scale scans may require larger DKI constraint weights than high-SNR token settings.

condition: Any Cholesky-parameterized DTI dataset where the tensor is already positive definite by construction
model: Do not add model complexity solely to enforce tensor positivity.
data: Use denoising and normalization choices to stabilize signal fitting rather than extra positivity handling.
training: Keep optimization focused on reconstruction stability with AdamW and clipping.
loss: Set extra physics constraint weight to zero or near-zero by default.
Use reconstruction and light robust terms instead of redundant positive-definiteness penalties.
boundary: This does not apply to DKI kurtosis validity constraints or NODDI parameter-range constraints.
If implementation-specific outputs can violate the Cholesky positivity transform, revisit this assumption.
